item.title: Israeli election to test Benjamin Netanyahu's ability to hold power
item.description:
Tens of thousands marched in Tel Aviv last night demanding Benjamin Netanyahu's government answer for the failures that led to the October 7 terror attacks. "We cannot be a dictatorship!" said one woman. "And we cannot have these criminals running our country."
Tens of thousands participated in an anti-government demonstration, demanding a state commission of enquiry into the October 7 attacks, at the Hostages Square in Tel Aviv, October 24, 2026, ahead of Israel's parliamentary election Tuesday.
Jack GUEZ/AFP via Getty Images
Tuesday will be the first parliamentary elections since the attacks. Thirty-nine parties are running, but essentially one man is on the ballot: Netanyahu. Over three decades, Netanyahu (known here as Bibi) has dominated Israeli politics.
And in a market outside Tel Aviv, opinions about the prime minister are as varied as the offerings here.
Asked whom he will vote for, restaurant owner Benny Abraham replied, "Likud and Bibi Netanyahu."
"Bibi can handle the whole world," Abraham said. "Bibi is charismatic. He has a strong voice. The world loves him." He added affectionately, "He's the king of Israel."
Many others, like Liat and her husband Sharon, could be lumped into the "Anyone but Bibi" camp. "I don't hate him, OK, I think he did the good things to Israel, but no more," said Liat.
Sharon described Netanyahu as "more or less, very good politician, but not a [good manager]."
The divide on Netanyhu stems from controversial changes sidelining the country's judiciary; an ongoing trial on corruption charges; and allegations he failed to heed prior warnings about October 7.

item.title: Iran says potential new U.S. strikes won't change Tehran's position
item.description:
What to know about the Iran war today: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Sunday that a potential resumption of war with Israel and the U.S. would not change his country's positions, after President Trump said Washington "may do another little Epic Fury."Iran warned on Saturday that U.S. ships would never be allowed in the Persian Gulf "under any circumstances," as tensions between Tehran and Washington continue mounting. Both sides have signaled a possible return to strikes, with the U.S. ambassador to Turkey warning Iran could be struck as soon as this weekend.Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned Friday that Iran has "substantially increased efforts to target U.S. personnel" abroad, with plots to kill Americans reaching "advanced stages" in the Middle East and other countries.
New Updates
7:13 AM
Iran's parliament speaker calls on people to reduce use of natural gas
Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf on Sunday called for a campaign to cut gas consumption by at least 10%, with officials anticipating shortages as winter approaches.
While a major producer, Iran has long suffered shortages of natural gas, essential for powering heating systems, which have been exacerbated by war with the United States and Israel that began in February.
During the most intense phase of the fighting, which lasted nearly 40 days, the two countries struck key Iranian infrastructure including natural gas refineries, according to Tehran.
Winter in Iran often sees temperatures drop below freezing, especially in the country's north.

item.title: Kim Jong Un visits China to open new bridge, reaffirm ties
item.description:
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un visited China on Saturday, inaugurating a new bridge that connects the two countries and vowing to expand cooperation with his powerful neighbor.
Kim's visit to China, the first in a year, is his latest move in an increasingly assertive foreign policy as he seeks to align Pyongyang with Beijing and Moscow in a united front against the United States under what he portrays as a "new Cold War."
Kim arrived in the Chinese border city of Dandong Saturday after crossing the newly opened bridge, according to South Korea's Unification Ministry and China's official Xinhua News Agency.
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, alongside Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, during a see-off ceremony at the new Yalu River Bridge, on Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026. (Rao Aimin/Xinhua via AP)
Rao Aimin
In Dandong, Kim visited a memorial marking China's support of North Korea during the 1950-53 Korean War and met with Wang Huning, a member of the Standing Committee of China's Communist Party.
At the memorial, Kim said that the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK) will "firmly carry forward the invincible DPRK-China friendship forged at the cost of blood all the time," according to the North's official Korean Central News Agency.
During their meeting, Kim reaffirmed a resolve to develop bilateral cooperation, while Wang conveyed Chinese President Xi Jinping's greetings and said Kim's visit to the memorial was "of great significance" in carrying forward the friendship between the two countries, KCNA said.

item.title: More than 1,000 arrested in France as protesters and police clash
item.description:
Police made 1,314 arrests in nationwide protests in France, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said Sunday, after demonstrations over the high cost of living and the country's education system earlier in the day remained largely peaceful.
Nuñez 53 officers were hurt in marches. He said on Saturday marches "passed off well" in cities, but police officers found themselves confronted with "an extremely elevated level of violence" from "ultra-left" groups later in the day. Nuñez said some shops and businesses had been looted, but "the scale was far smaller" than a week earlier, when some 3,000 businesses were damaged or looted.
He said police acted more rapidly and conducted more pre-demonstration checks. Businesses and shopping centers had also been better protected. Earlier Saturday, the interior minister said police had confiscated weapons including metal balls, lead pellets, fireworks, slingshots, steel balls, improvised weapons, a katana and airsoft weapons, he said.
The French Interior Ministry said about 410,000 people participated in about 298 protests around the country. Union organizers from the General Confederation of Labor put the number at around 800,000. An explanation for the discrepancy was not immediately available.
A protester waves the French flag near Porte de Vincennes during a demonstration in Paris on October 24, 2026.
Aris MESSINIS /AFP via Getty Images
Some confrontations were reported between authorities and demonstrators in several cities, but as of Saturday evening there had been no repeat of the major street violence and rioting that erupted amid similar protests last week.

item.title: 1 arrested after fire at Hitler's Eagle's Nest mountain retreat
item.description:
A suspect has been arrested in Germany following a fire at Adolf Hitler's mountain retreat, known as Eagle's Nest, German police said.
Authorities were alerted to a fire at the Nazi leader's mountain residence on the peak of Obersalzberg at approximately 9:15 p.m. local time on Friday, Upper Bavaria South police said in a statement.
The building, also known as Kehlsteinhaus, was "completely engulfed in flames" when firefighters arrived, police said, but no one was found inside and no injuries were reported.
Fire trucks had some difficulty accessing the site "due to the local conditions," authorities added.
Still from a webcam of the Kehlsteinhaus early on Oct. 24, 2026, after a large fire broke out in the southern German state of Bavaria.
Berchtesgaden /AFP via Getty Images
"Shortly after the fire broke out, a suspect came into the focus of investigators," the statement said, adding that the cause of the fire is now under criminal investigation and one person was taken into custody.
The 33-year-old suspect, a German citizen who has ties to the Berchtesgaden area but doesn't currently live there, prosecutors said, has been questioned, The Associated Press reported. They said he showed signs of mental illness and he was being sent to a psychiatric facility, but they also would look into the possibility of a political motive in view of the building's history.
There were no current indications that anyone else was involved, police said.
At an elevation of 6,017 feet, Hitler's Eagle's Nest was completed in 1938 and occasionally used by the Nazi leader as a temporary seat of government. The site was spared from Allied bombing during World War II, largely preserving its original state.

item.title: Elon Musk says SpaceX throttled Ukraine Starlink speeds over drone strikes
item.description:
Elon Musk said on Saturday that his company SpaceX had throttled the Starlink satellite internet service in Ukraine, disrupting operations that the country relies on to defend itself against Russia.
Musk's admission on social media came after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that Ukraine's access to Starlink and Starshield satellite links has been restored to the speeds it had before restrictions that disrupted front-line operations for more than a week.
Questions have persisted since last week about who ordered the interruptions to the Musk-made satellite internet system that Kyiv has relied on for years to counter Moscow's attacks.
"The speeds are now where they need to be," Zelenskyy wrote on X, adding that restoration began overnight and were sufficient by Saturday morning, improving front-line logistics and defense against Russian jet-powered Shahed drones.
President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv on Oct. 22, 2026.
Ukrinform/NurPhoto via Getty Images
Musk admits he was behind Starlink's speed restriction
Before Musk's confirmation, questions persisted last week about who ordered the interruptions to the Musk-made satellite internet system that Ukraine has relied on for years to counter Moscow's attacks.
President Trump had said he didn't make the call, while also saying Musk should not be blamed. On Tuesday, CBS News reported that Musk was behind the disruption.
In a post Saturday on X, Musk acknowledged that his company SpaceX throttled the Starlink satellite internet service.
